title: Fixed-beta mixture-seminorm orbit-contract stress test
question: Can the beta,# contractivity assumed by the finite-member Duhamel bridge be inferred from a fixed-beta mixture state without first proving the finite Hamiltonian-to-OS embedding?
method: Use an exact polarized 2x2 density matrix rho and a rational 3-4-5 unitary orbit generated by a noncommuting Hamiltonian direction.
Evaluate the same two-sided psi(X*X)+psi(XX*) seminorm on P_- before and after conjugation, retaining the exact rational growth gap.
Check the finite witness independently and in Lean, then keep the obstruction scoped to automatic contractivity rather than rejecting invariant OS dynamics.
finding: For rho=(I+(3/5)sigma_z)/2, U=(3I-4i sigma_x)/5 and P_-=(I-sigma_z)/2, the initial two-sided squared seminorm is 2/5 while the conjugated value is 146/125, with exact growth gap 96/125. Therefore a fixed mixture state does not automatically make a noncommuting finite Hamiltonian orbit beta,# contractive.
decision_reason: This adversarial checkpoint isolates the missing finite Hamiltonian-to-OS invariant embedding required by EXP-001062; it does not reject the OS-reconstructed group or the Q3 route.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite stress test. It does not prove or disprove actual Q3 operator history, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, exhaustion, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, common alpha, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or the TECT production owner.
